newsitem.title: CHILE: Placido Domingo has bronchitis, stops Chile concert.
newsitem.headline: Placido Domingo has bronchitis, stops Chile concert.

text.p: Spanish tenor Placido Domingo broke off his concert in a packed Chilean theatre on Tuesday night after just two arias, saying that bronchitis kept him from continuing.
Fans speculated that Domingo's bronchitis may have been caused by the high levels of smog in the city that suffers some of the world's worst air pollution.
"I don't know what it was. I know I arrived well and the next day I didn't feel well," Domingo said on Wednesday as he left his hotel to go to Santiago's airport.
"It may have been the smog, the central heating. The combination meant I wasn't at my best," he said.

Domingo abandoned the concert at Santiago's Municipal Theatre after just half an hour, disappointing some 1,500 opera fans who had bought tickets to the recital with Chilean soprano Veronica Villarroel months ago.
"It is not fair for you or me to continue singing in these conditions," Domingo said after the second aria in the concert organised to commemorate his first visit to Chile 30 years ago.
The tenor said he was planning to return to Chile at the end of the month to finish his recital.

"I feel sorry because of the enthusiasm of the public with this theatre full of flowers, but I want to return and we are trying to fix a date," he said in his dressing room where he was visited after the concert by dozens of fans, including President Eduardo Frei.
Domingo often sings solo or accompanied by fellow Spaniard Jose Carreras and Italian Luciano Pavarotti in a series of concerts that have become known as the Three Tenors.
